hypothesis: The input validation logic for minutesOffset was too restrictive, incorrectly rejecting negative values that are valid when the hoursOffset is zero or negative. The fix expands the allowed range for minutesOffset and adds a specific check to prevent invalid combinations (positive hours with negative minutes).
prediction: The code will now allow minutesOffset values between -59 and 59, and include a conditional check to ensure that if hoursOffset is positive, minutesOffset cannot be negative.
experiment_rationale: The fix diff shows the modification of the range check for minutesOffset from (minutesOffset < 0 || minutesOffset > 59) to (minutesOffset < -59 || minutesOffset > 59), and the addition of a new guard clause to handle the sign consistency between hours and minutes. This confirms the root cause was an incorrect validation predicate.
reasoning_summary: The bug is fundamentally a validation error. The original code used an overly restrictive conditional check (Checking) that failed to account for valid negative minute offsets. The fix involves modifying the conditional logic (the range check) and adding a new guard clause, which is the hallmark of a Checking defect.
